title: 第四章 滴水痕
content_zh:
接下来的日子，像山涧里淌过的水，看似无声，却在石头上留下细微的、日积月累的痕迹。

    陈默的日常依旧被精确地切割成块：寅时三刻起床，冷水擦身，站桩。卯时上山砍柴，柴刀比往日快了两分，砍倒同样粗细的树干，能省下小半炷香的时间。辰时到午时，是杂役院派下的各种活计，挑水、清扫、搬运，单调而繁重。午时一刻吃饭，饭后他不再去废料场，而是寻了个更僻静的角落，尝试那依旧渺茫的气感。未时到申时，继续劳作。申时三刻到酉时，雷打不动的炼气吐纳。酉时到戌时，是《基础淬体术》的九个动作，他如今已能完整做完两组，虽然每个动作都做得龇牙咧嘴，大汗淋漓。戌时之后，或是借着最后的天光翻看那本快被翻烂的《引气诀》，或是在油灯下（需自己掏钱买灯油，他半月才舍得点一次）用捡来的炭笔，在日课纸的背面，记录一些模糊的感受。

    比如：“三月初七，夜，气感于丹田左下游移，行至膻中受阻，盘旋约二十息，退。较前日凝实一线。”

    字迹工整，力透纸背，但记录的内容却贫瘠得可怜。二十息，不过常人三十次呼吸的时间，那股暖流便无力为继。但陈默写得很认真，仿佛那不是一丝随时会消散的温热，而是某种确凿无疑的进境。

    磨刀成了新的日课。每隔三五日，他便在戌时之后，带上柴刀和三块石头，到那背风的屋檐下。先用粗石打掉明显的钝口和毛刺，再用青石细磨，最后用那块细腻的深色石头抛光开刃。磨刀的声音“嗤嗤”或“沙沙”，混杂在风声虫鸣里，成了黑夜固定的背景音。那半截断剑也被他磨出了一小段锋口，虽然锈迹难除，但偶尔用来削削木棍，倒也顺手。

    变化是缓慢的，几乎无法察觉。柴刀的刃口越来越亮，挥砍时越发省力。站桩时，双腿颤抖的时间推迟了那么十几息。《基础淬体术》的动作，似乎能做得更到位一点，拉伸时肌肉筋腱的酸痛感，也略微习惯了那么一丝。丹田里的那缕气感，出现得依旧艰难，停滞的位置也依旧牢固，但每次盘桓的时间，似乎真的在极其缓慢地增加。从二十息，到二十五息，到三十息……

    只是这点细微的不同，放在每日重复的、沉重的劳作里，放在那些看不见尽头的砍柴、挑水、清理杂草中，几乎可以忽略不计。他还是那个沉默寡言、背着巨大柴捆在山道上缓慢行走的四灵根杂役，是灶房里坐在角落、仔细刮净碗底食物残渣的穷小子。管事赵胖子看他的眼神依旧懒散，同院的杂役们依旧为多一口吃食、少干一点活计而争吵不休。主峰上的灯火与乐声，依旧遥远得像个不真切的梦。

    直到那场雨。

    清明刚过，连绵的春雨就来了，一下就是七八天。不大，但细密冰冷，无孔不入。杂役院的屋子年久失修，多处漏雨，通铺里弥漫着一股潮湿的霉味和汗馊气混合的怪味。不少杂役都染了风寒，咳嗽声此起彼伏。王虎也病了，烧得满脸通红，裹着那床薄被瑟瑟发抖，连去灶房领饭的力气都没有。

    陈默每日的活计也因此变得更加艰难。山路湿滑，背着湿柴下山，一步三滑。挑水的井台边积满了泥浆，木桶也格外沉重。冰冷的雨水灌进草鞋，脚趾冻得麻木，到了夜里放在被窝里回暖，又痒又痛。连那背风的屋檐下也积了水，他只能缩在门廊更深处站桩、吐纳，寒意更甚。

    这日午后，雨势稍歇，但天色依旧阴沉得厉害。陈默被派去清理后山一条被落叶和断枝堵塞的排水沟。沟不深，但很长，里面满是腐叶、淤泥和不知名的虫豸。他用一柄豁口的铁锹，一锹一锹地将腥臭的污泥铲到沟边。雨水将他的头发、衣服全都打湿，紧紧贴在身上，冰冷刺骨。

    清理了约莫一半，铁锹“铛”一声，碰到了硬物。

    陈默停下，用锹拨开污泥，发现是一块半埋在沟底的青石板，石板边缘平整，像是人工凿刻的。他用力将石板撬开一角，下面黑洞洞的，似乎是个不大的空洞，一股更浓的陈腐气味涌了上来。

    他蹲下身，用手扒开周围的淤泥，发现石板下是一个尺许见方、深约两尺的凹坑。坑底积着浑浊的泥水，隐约能看到水底沉着什么东西。

    陈默用铁锹将坑底的泥水舀出一些，待水稍清，才看清那似乎是几块碎瓦，一个生满绿锈、看不出原样的金属小件，还有……一个沾满泥污的、巴掌大的布囊。

    布囊是用某种厚实的粗布缝制的，已经被泥水浸泡得发黑发硬，但口子用麻绳紧紧扎着，似乎还没完全烂透。

    陈默用铁锹小心地将布囊拨弄出来，放在沟边的石头上。他先清理了周围的淤泥，确保排水沟通畅，然后才拿起那个沉甸甸、湿漉漉的布囊。

    麻绳已经朽烂，一扯就断。他打开布囊，里面没有他预想中的金银或灵石，只有几样零碎东西：一把生了厚厚铜绿的小钥匙，一个边缘磕破的粗陶小瓶，瓶塞已经烂掉，里面空空如也；还有两本用油布仔细包裹着的小册子。

    油布防水，里面的册子虽然边缘受潮卷曲，但字迹大致还能看清。

    陈默拿起第一本，很薄，封皮上没有字。他小心地翻开，里面是密密麻麻的蝇头小楷，墨色已有些褪色，但工整清晰。开篇写道：
content_en:
The days that followed were like water flowing in a mountain stream, seemingly silent, but leaving tiny traces on the stone that accumulate over time.
Chen Mo's daily life is still cut into precise pieces: getting up at three o'clock in the morning, rubbing himself with cold water, and standing still.When I went up the mountain to chop firewood, my hatchet was two minutes faster than before. Cutting down tree trunks of the same thickness could save half the time of burning incense.From Chen time to noon, there are various tasks assigned by the handyman courtyard, such as carrying water, cleaning, and transportation, which are monotonous and arduous.He had dinner at a quarter of noon. After the meal, he no longer went to the scrapyard, but found a more secluded corner to try the still vague sense of energy.When the time is not yet due, continue working.When the third quarter of the Shen hour arrives at the You hour, he can refining his Qi and exhaling it without any hesitation.From Youshi to Xushi, there are nine movements in "Basic Body Tempering Technique". He has now been able to complete two sets of them completely, although he grimaced and sweated profusely in each movement.After hours, he would either take advantage of the last daylight to read the almost torn-up book "Qi Entraining Art", or use the charcoal he picked up under an oil lamp (he had to pay for lamp oil himself, and he was only willing to light it once every half a month) to record some vague feelings on the back of the daily class paper.
For example: "On the night of the seventh day of March, the Qi moved to the left and lower reaches of the Dantian. When it reached the Tanzhong, it was blocked. It circled for about twenty breaths and then retreated. It was a little more solid than the day before."
The handwriting is neat and strong, but the recorded content is pitifully barren.Twenty breaths is no more than thirty breaths for an ordinary person, and that warm current is no longer able to continue.But Chen Mo wrote very seriously, as if it was not a trace of warmth that could dissipate at any time, but some kind of unmistakable progress.
Knife sharpening became the new daily routine.Every three to five days, after Xu Shi, he would take a hatchet and three stones and go to the eaves of the leeward house.First use a rough stone to remove the obvious blunt edges and burrs, then use a bluestone to finely grind it, and finally use the fine dark stone to polish and sharpen it.The sound of sharpening a knife, "chichi" or "rustle", mixed with the sound of wind and insects, became a fixed background sound in the dark night.He also sharpened a small edge on the half-cut sword. Although the rust was difficult to remove, it was still handy for sharpening wooden sticks occasionally.
The change is slow and almost imperceptible.The blade of the hatchet is getting brighter and brighter, making it easier to slash with less effort.When standing still, the trembling of my legs was delayed for more than ten breaths.The movements of "Basic Body Tempering Technique" seem to be a little better, and the soreness of muscles and tendons during stretching has become slightly accustomed to it.The feeling of Qi in Dantian is still difficult to appear, and the stagnation position is still firm, but the time it lingers every time seems to be increasing extremely slowly.From twenty breaths, to twenty-five breaths, to thirty breaths...
It's just this subtle difference that can be almost ignored in the daily repetitive and heavy work, in the endless tasks of chopping wood, carrying water, and clearing weeds.He is still the taciturn Silinggen handyman who walks slowly on the mountain road carrying a huge bundle of firewood. He is also the poor boy who sits in the corner of the kitchen and carefully scrapes the food residue from the bottom of the bowl.The steward, Fatty Zhao, still looked at him with lazy eyes, and the handymen in the same courtyard were still quarreling over an extra bite of food and a little less work.The lights and music on the main peak are still as distant as an unreal dream.
Until that rain.
Just after the Qingming Festival, the continuous spring rain came, lasting for seven or eight days.Not big, but dense, cold, and pervasive.The house in the utility yard was in disrepair for a long time, and there were many leaks. The shop was filled with a strange smell of damp musty and sweaty smell.Many of the handymen had caught wind and cold, and they coughed one after another.Wang Hu was also sick, his face was red with fever, he was shivering wrapped in the thin quilt, and he didn't even have the strength to go to the kitchen to get food.
Chen Mo's daily work has become more difficult as a result.The mountain road is slippery, and carrying wet firewood down the mountain is slippery every step of the way.The side of the well platform for carrying water was filled with mud, and the wooden barrel was extremely heavy.The cold rain poured into the straw sandals, and my toes were numb from the cold. When I put them in bed to warm up at night, they felt itchy and painful.There was water even under the eaves of the leeward house. He could only huddle deeper in the porch to stand and breathe, and the chill became even worse.
In the afternoon of this day, the rain stopped slightly, but the sky was still very gloomy.Chen Mo was sent to clean up a drainage ditch blocked by fallen leaves and broken branches in the back hill.The ditch was not deep, but very long. It was filled with rotting leaves, silt and unknown insects.He used a gapped shovel to shovel the smelly mud to the edge of the ditch.The rain soaked his hair and clothes, clinging tightly to his body and making him feel bitingly cold.
After cleaning about half of it, the shovel made a clang sound and hit something hard.
Chen Mo stopped, used a shovel to push away the mud, and found a bluestone slab half buried at the bottom of the ditch. The edge of the slab was flat, as if it had been carved manually.He pried open a corner of the stone slab with force. The bottom was dark and seemed to be a small hole, and a stronger stale smell came up.
He squatted down and used his hands to peel away the surrounding mud, and found that under the stone slab was a pit about a foot square and about two feet deep.There was turbid muddy water at the bottom of the pit, and something could be vaguely seen at the bottom.
Chen Mo used a shovel to scoop out some of the muddy water at the bottom of the pit. When the water cleared a little, he saw clearly that it seemed to be a few broken tiles, a small metal piece that was covered with green rust and could not be seen as it was, and... a palm-sized cloth bag covered in mud.
The bag was sewn with some kind of thick coarse cloth, which had been soaked in mud and water until it became black and hard. However, the opening was tightly tied with hemp rope, and it seemed that it was not completely rotten.
Chen Mo carefully took out the cloth bag with a shovel and placed it on the stone beside the ditch.He first cleaned up the surrounding mud and ensured that the drainage channels were clear before picking up the heavy, wet cloth bag.
The hemp rope was rotten and would break when pulled.He opened the bag and found that there was no gold, silver or spiritual stones as he expected, only a few odds and ends: a small key with a thick patina, a small stoneware bottle with a chipped edge, the cork had rotted, and there was nothing inside; and two small booklets carefully wrapped in oilcloth.
The oilcloth is waterproof, and although the edges of the booklet inside are curled up due to moisture, the writing can still be read roughly.
Chen Mo picked up the first book. It was very thin and there was no writing on the cover.He carefully opened it, and inside was a dense collection of small regular script. The ink color had faded a little, but it was neat and clear.The opening paragraph reads:
